skill.name: summon-daem0n
skill.description: Guides agents through Daem0n-MCP setup for single repositories, linked repositories, consolidated memory stores, hooks, search, and indexing.
skill.summary: Set up and manage Daem0n-MCP project memory across repository layouts.
skill.author: DasBluEyedDevil

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown backtick false positives, but the skill includes real risky setup guidance. Confirmed issues include destructive deletion of a hidden memory directory, hidden memory data handling, and persistent Claude hook commands that execute local Python scripts automatically.

remediation.suggestion: Replace rm -rf guidance with an archive or rename workflow, require explicit confirmation, and scope examples to user-provided project paths.

remediation.issue: Automatic hook commands run local scripts from $HOME
remediation.suggestion: Make hook setup opt-in, document exactly what each script reads and writes, and require users to inspect scripts before enabling them.

remediation.issue: Hidden project memory can contain sensitive context
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before copying, consolidating, or indexing .daem0nmcp data, and recommend redaction or exclusion rules for secrets.

remediation.issue: Automatic memory capture lacks a clear consent boundary
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit opt-in instructions, disable automatic capture by default, and describe how to review and delete captured memories.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Hook Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to place hooks in .claude/settings.json that run Python scripts from $HOME during PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and Stop events. This can execute local code automatically whenever the agent edits files or ends a turn.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The hook configuration directly names command hooks and local Python scripts for repeated agent events. The risk is contextual persistence and automatic execution, not just the presence of a shell command.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Conversation and Decision Capture
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes a Silent Scribe that listens, parses words, and automatically records decisions. This can persist sensitive project context or conversation content without a clear opt-in boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose explicitly states that the tool listens, parses words, and inscribes decisions automatically. There is no evidence of external exfiltration, so the finding is limited to local privacy and data retention risk.

content.value_statement: Teams lose context when work spans several repositories or long sessions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a setup guide for shared Daem0n-MCP memory.
actual_capabilities: Explains single repository initialization for Daem0n-MCP.
Compares consolidated parent memory with linked separate repository memory.
Shows how to consolidate linked databases and archive source stores.
Documents hook-based memory capture for edit and stop events.
Summarizes condensed recall, hybrid search tuning, tagging, and indexing features.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install Daem0n-MCP by itself.
Several examples use placeholder absolute paths that must be adapted before use.
Some instructions involve hidden project memory directories and destructive cleanup commands.
Hook setup depends on local scripts under the user home directory.

use_cases.description: Plan a shared Daem0n-MCP parent store for related backend and frontend repositories.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Project Memory
use_cases.description: Review an existing Daem0n-MCP store and choose whether to preserve, consolidate, or archive it.

use_cases.title: Tune Recall and Indexing Behavior
use_cases.description: Apply condensed recall, hybrid search weights, tags, and indexing checks to improve retrieval quality.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Single Repo Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the summon-daem0n skill to explain how I should initialize Daem0n-MCP for this repository. Include any safety checks first.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Multi-Repo Layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare parent consolidation with linked separate histories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the summon-daem0n skill to compare consolidated parent memory and linked separate memory for my backend and client repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Memory Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Move from a messy existing store to a cleaner structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the summon-daem0n skill to create a migration plan for an existing Daem0n-MCP store. Avoid destructive steps unless I approve them.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Hooks and Search Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of automation and retrieval behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the summon-daem0n skill to review hook setup, automatic memory capture, condensed recall, search weighting, and indexing settings for risk and usefulness.

output_examples.input: I have backend and client repositories under one parent folder.
output_examples.output: Recommended layout: use the parent folder as the shared memory root, link both child repositories, consolidate only after backup, then verify the combined memory count.

output_examples.input: My existing memory store is noisy and may contain stale decisions.
output_examples.output: Recommended migration: back up the existing store, inspect recent decisions and statistics, preserve useful entries, and avoid deleting the store without explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Recall returns too many long results for broad searches.
output_examples.output: Recommended tuning: use condensed recall for broad surveys, adjust hybrid search weighting for the project, and limit repeated results from the same file.

best_practices: Back up project memory before consolidation, migration, or cleanup.
Use one shared memory root only when repositories belong to the same logical project.
Review hook commands and data retention behavior before enabling automatic capture.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive cleanup commands against hidden memory directories without confirmation.
Do not enable automatic hooks from unreviewed local scripts.
Do not consolidate unrelated repositories into one memory store.

faq.question: Does this skill install Daem0n-MCP?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and command examples for an existing Daem0n-MCP environment.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both shared parent memory and linked separate memory for related repositories.

faq.question: Does it require shell access?
faq.answer: Some examples use shell commands for navigation, backup, cleanup, and CLI usage.

faq.question: Are the hook examples safe to enable automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review the local hook scripts and data retention behavior before enabling automatic command hooks.

faq.question: What data can Daem0n-MCP store?
faq.answer: The skill describes memory for decisions, rationale, file paths, tags, search indexes, and related project context.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools for this documentation skill.
